items.title: Physical Intelligence Reportedly Seeks $1B at a $20B Valuation
items.summary: Physical Intelligence is reportedly seeking at least $1 billion in funding with a valuation around $20 billion. This discussion coincides with the company opening its models to outside developers via an API beta for training and inference. Existing investors Avenir and Lux Capital are reportedly in talks to lead the financing round. The API allows developers to use PI's models and infrastructure to build applications, reflecting a focus on a shared intelligence layer across different robot bodies. The company aims to create a foundation model by learning across diverse robot experiences.

The company has made its models available to external developers through an API beta for training and inference purposes. This access facilitates the development of applications utilizing Physical Intelligence's models and infrastructure, emphasizing a shared intelligence layer across various robot bodies. items.title: AGIBOT Introduces Worken, New AI Models and G2 Max at Innovation Day 2026
items.summary: AGIBOT introduced Worken, a framework to measure robot productivity using the formula: Worken = Active Robots × Autonomous Working Hours × Output Efficiency Ratio. The company showcased new hardware like AHA3, which integrates locomotion, interaction, and task execution capabilities. New AI models include GO-3 Preview for reasoning and prediction, and WITA-Omni 1.0 for human-robot interaction. The G2 Max robot is designed for industrial handling with a 40 kg capacity and adjustable working height. Furthermore, Link-U OS 1.0 is being developed with an open-source roadmap, aiming for full open-sourcing by the end of 2026.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "AGIBOT Introduces Worken, New AI Models and G2 Max at Innovation Day 2026". This report details the unveiling of new AI models, hardware, and productivity frameworks at the Innovation Day 2026 event. The company introduced Worken, a metric for robot productivity calculated by the formula Worken equals Active Robots times Autonomous Working Hours times the Output Efficiency Ratio. Demonstrations included new hardware such as the AHA3, which incorporates locomotion, interaction, and task execution functions, alongside new AI models including GO-3 Preview for reasoning and prediction and WITA-Omni 1.0 for human-robot interaction. The G2 Max robot was presented, designed for industrial handling with a forty kilogram capacity and an adjustable working height. Additionally, the Link-U OS 1.0 is under development with an open-source roadmap intended for full open-sourcing by the close of 2026. This development signals advancements in measurable robotics and human-robot collaboration technologies.

items.title: Maxinsights raises $30 million to build training data platform for physical AI
items.summary: Maxinsights raised $30 million to expand its physical AI data platform, which generates training data by paying contractors to record real-world activities. The company has collected over 2 million hours of human activity, with 1.5 million hours being model-ready for AI applications. They utilize systems like MaxLoop for quality control and MaxGlove to capture tactile information, such as grip force. This real-world data collection method is designed to expose AI models to the variations found in actual homes and workplaces. Maxinsights serves over 30 customers, including AI labs and foundation model developers.

items.title: What Symbotic’s Walmart growth teaches robotics startups about anchor customers
items.summary: Symbotic's dependence on Walmart as a major customer highlights the need for robotics startups to scrutinize anchor customer relationships. Understanding contract terms, such as continuity rights and sales limitations, is crucial for assessing the true cost of servicing large accounts. Growth strategy should focus on understanding the field-load logic, where pilot programs can reveal hidden field work costs and support needs. Startups should aim to build repeatable processes that minimize the dependency on single anchor customers for future demand. Ultimately, founders should model scenarios to determine growth potential while prioritizing contractual control and financial resilience over sheer customer volume.

items.title: Unitree’s Quarterly Revenue Surges 70% as R&D Spending Weighs on Profit
items.summary: Unitree reported third-quarter revenue of 665 million yuan, a 70% year-on-year increase, alongside a sharp rise in research spending. Net profit attributable to shareholders decreased by 17.4% to 112.7 million yuan. Research and development spending surged by 249.6% to 127 million yuan, focusing on embodied-intelligence models and computing capacity. Although profitable, earnings did not keep pace with revenue growth due to significant development costs. Overall, the results highlight substantial sales expansion concurrent with heavy investment in future technology.

items.title: WorldOracle Tests Whether World Models Can Reliably Predict Real-World Executions
items.summary: WorldOracle is a benchmark designed to evaluate action-conditioned world models by comparing their predictions against real-world executions from the same starting conditions and action sequences. The evaluation assesses how accurately models predict object positions, movements, and the consequences of actions, including failures. Results showed that while robot arm motion was often predicted reasonably well, object positions frequently deviated from reality, and performance degraded over longer operational sequences. The benchmark utilizes multiple scoring metrics, such as Physical State Correctness and Interaction Spatial Alignment, to dissect prediction errors. Developers can participate by submitting predictions from open-weight or closed-source models to receive concrete feedback for model improvement.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "WorldOracle Tests Whether World Models Can Reliably Predict Real-World Executions". This report evaluates action-conditioned world models by comparing their predictions against real-world executions under identical starting conditions and action sequences. The evaluation assessed the models' accuracy in predicting object positions, movements, and the consequences of actions, including instances of failure. The benchmark utilized multiple scoring metrics, including Physical State Correctness and Interaction Spatial Alignment, to detail prediction errors. Results indicated that while predictions regarding robot arm motion were often reasonable, object positions frequently differed from actual reality, and performance diminished across extended operational sequences. Developers can contribute by submitting predictions from various model types to receive specific feedback for model refinement. This research highlights ongoing challenges in achieving precise, long-term prediction in dynamic physical environments for artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Audi Tests Agile Robots’ Mobile Humanoids for Automotive Parts Sequencing
items.summary: Audi is testing Agile Robots’ mobile humanoids to handle parts sequencing at its Ingolstadt Production Lab. The project aims for the robots to pick components from containers and arrange them for automotive assembly. Agile Robots provides the mobile humanoids, while Dassault Systèmes and NVIDIA support virtual testing using a virtual twin. The system incorporates dual-arm manipulation and a mobile base to handle varied, unsorted components in logistics environments. Future success will depend on demonstrating consistent physical performance and operational costs.

items.title: Neura Robotics and TUM open €17 million RoboGym and unveil new humanoid
items.summary: Neura Robotics and the Technical University of Munich opened a €17 million robotics center and unveiled the 4NE1 humanoid robot. This facility, the TUM RoboGym, combines research, training, and industrial applications for various sectors. The center trains robots in tasks like handling boxes and loading components using real-world data, human demonstrations, and simulation. The new 4NE1 Gen 4 humanoid robot is lighter and features advanced "Smart Limbs" powered by Neuron AI. This initiative aims to advance physical AI capabilities and establish an international network of such training facilities.

items.title: Xpeng Iron batteries enter small batch output ahead of robot
items.summary: Batteries for the Xpeng Iron humanoid robot have entered small batch production, though the robot itself is still pre-production. Xpeng's vice president announced this battery update at the SAE conference, describing a solid-state battery designed specifically for the robot's limited space. The battery is claimed to prevent thermal runaway spread and withstand impact testing. However, the exact battery chemistry remains unclear, with some reports suggesting solid-liquid hybrid technology was used due to commercialization delays. Xpeng still targets mass production of Iron by the end of 2026.

items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: Living digital twins, enhanced by AI, combine dynamic representations of industrial operations with real-time control to achieve synchronization. Agentic AI enables systems to move toward industrial homeostasis by making autonomous adjustments, while human oversight remains crucial to define operational goals and monitor AI alignment. This synchronization is achieved by linking real-time sensor data through a digital thread, incorporating predictive models and AI insights. Real-world applications show AI optimizing energy use, improving quality, and ensuring asset health across various industries. Future integration involves pairing physical AI with robotics to create interconnected industrial networks that enhance resilience.

items.title: North American robot orders climb 24.8% in Q3 of 2026, says A3
items.summary: North American robot orders increased by 24.8% in units and 26.1% in value in the third quarter of 2026. Total robot orders for the first nine months of 2026 reached 28,984 units valued at approximately $1.89 billion. Growth was driven by automotive, semiconductor, life sciences, and plastics/rubber sectors, showing a diversified market expansion. Collaborative robots also saw a strong increase of 56% in Q3, accounting for 16.7% of all units ordered. This positive momentum occurs alongside expanding manufacturing activity, positioning the market for continued growth.

items.title: Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing
items.summary: Faraday Future is transitioning its focus to building a US robotics business by establishing domestic manufacturing capabilities. The company plans to bring a US robot factory online by the end of 2026 and launch its first US-assembled robot in February 2027. This localization strategy aims to enhance supply-chain resilience, regulatory compliance, and quality control for its robotics products. Faraday Future sees vehicles and robotics as complementary parts of a larger physical AI ecosystem, sharing core technologies like AI and perception. Success will be measured by establishing a sustainable US-based physical AI and robotics ecosystem rather than just single metrics like revenue.

items.title: Robbyant’s Embodied AI Challenge Will Send 15 Teams to a Real-Robot Final in Shanghai
items.summary: Robbyant will advance 15 teams to a final competition in Shanghai, a 48-hour hackathon involving physical robots. Competitors will use AgileX Robotics’ Cobot Magic platform to adapt models to physical hardware. The challenge is based on the open-source LingBot-VLA 2.0 model, with over 1,800 teams having registered. Final task design and scoring criteria are still being finalized by Robbyant. The competition aims to measure how effectively vision-language-action models can be adapted to real-world robotic tasks.

items.title: A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine
items.summary: MIT engineers developed a robotic enteroscope to navigate the narrow small intestine for easier diagnosis and treatment. This soft robot is inspired by snake locomotion, using flexible actuators and specially coated surfaces for traction on the intestinal lining. The device is equipped with tools for imaging, drug delivery, and taking biopsies or removing polyps. Researchers aim to overcome the limitations of current procedures like double balloon enteroscopy for evaluating the long intestinal segment. Animal studies have successfully demonstrated the robot's movement and the functionality of its tools.

items.title: Warp Sciences emerges from stealth, to apply robotics to drug research
items.summary: Warp Sciences raised $215 million to create chemistry infrastructure for sovereign biotech, aiming to accelerate drug discovery. The company is building a U.S.-based contract research organization that integrates chemists, robotics, and AI to make and test molecules. The goal is to generate real-world data to train AI, enabling more capable labs and faster progression from hypothesis to experiment. Warp focuses on lead optimization analog synthesis, allowing customers to maintain control over sensitive research within the U.S. through automation. The company's team brings expertise in AI, healthcare, and robotics to this mission.

items.title: Welcome, W-Bot!
items.summary: Yue Quan Bionics created a wheeled humanoid robot featuring a compact base and an articulated upper body for tight space manipulation. Standing 178 cm tall and weighing 60 kg, it utilizes folding joints to achieve a working reach from floor level to 2.2 meters. The robot is equipped with multiple arms capable of lifting 10 kg and sensory systems including depth cameras and LiDAR for environmental awareness. Its primary capabilities focus on obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and product assembly within constrained areas. Produced by Yue Quan Bionics, the robot offers a practical design prioritizing reach and compact positioning over full locomotion.

items.title: Welcome, CYBORG H02!
items.summary: CYBORG H02 is a robotic hand manufactured by Cyborg Robotics in Guangdong, China. It features a design based on five fingers and a tendon mechanism driven by six electric motors. The hand weighs 750 grams and has dimensions of 248 × 114 × 52 millimeters. It has a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of 7/10, with a Degrees of Freedom rating of 3/5 and a Strength rating of 4/5. The product is currently in production with an advertised price of USD 4,000.

items.title: Welcome, Mornine!
items.summary: Mornine is a 167 cm tall, 70 kg bipedal humanoid developed by AiMOGA for commercial settings. It features an aluminum alloy structure, electric joint actuators, and five fingers on each hand, offering 40 degrees of freedom. The robot can perform obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, with a maximum speed of 3.6 km/h and a 3 kg strength capacity. It has a low Humanoid Guide Skill Score of 2/10, indicating early-stage physical capabilities in navigation and manipulation. Mornine is currently in production in China with a listed price of approximately US$41,400.

items.title: Welcome, NE01!
items.summary: NE01 is a 145 cm tall, 40 kg humanoid robot developed by GENISOM AI, designed for research, commercial use, and tourism. It features an aluminum alloy structure with integrated joint modules and a 540 watt hour battery providing a two-hour runtime. The robot has demonstrated capabilities in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, though navigation and manipulation skills are rated very low. Despite its design ambition, NE01 is currently understood as a preliminary platform rather than a broadly capable worker. The robot is listed as a prototype with an indicative price of $20,000 USD.
